headline: Histology guides inference of continuous, large-panel and higher-resolution spatial gene expression
label: Histology Anchored Spatial Expression Reconstruction
summary: New preprints use histology to extend sparse spatial transcriptomics into 3D and large gene panels, while others refine resolution and spatial statistics.
synthesis: The dominant thread uses histology as a scaffold to recover expression beyond what is measured. HIM-INR reconstructs continuous 3D expression from sparse spatial transcriptomics with a histology-informed multi-task implicit neural representation, and GeneFlow uses flow matching with histology and gene tokenizers to predict up to 1,000 genes. CroSP integrates expression, location and histology through cross-view contrastive graph learning. A second strand sharpens or analyzes resolution: st2sc infers single-cell profiles from multicellular spots, SpaAxFormer imputes with axial transformers, Spectrast casts spatial autocorrelation as FFT convolutions, and Spindle indexes co-expression for fast querying. GeneSPOT applies optimal transport to gene-relationship reorganization across conditions and time. SCALEMAP and Bloom address non-spatial multi-omics integration, and Sphinx addresses spatial proteomics neighborhoods.
